theory.overview: A Fenwick Tree (Binary Indexed Tree or BIT) is a data structure that efficiently supports prefix sum queries and point updates, both in O(log n) time. It uses less memory than segment trees (O(n) vs O(4n)) and has better cache performance due to simpler operations. The key insight is using binary representation of indices to store partial sums. BITs are ideal for problems requiring cumulative frequency tables or prefix sums with updates.

keyConcepts.name: Range of Responsibility
keyConcepts.description: Each index i is responsible for range [i - 2^r + 1, i] where r is position of least significant set bit. 2^r = i & (-i).

keyConcepts.name: Update Operation
keyConcepts.description: To add value at index i: while i <= n, tree[i] += value, i += i & (-i). Propagates up the tree.

keyConcepts.name: Query Operation
keyConcepts.description: To get prefix sum [1, i]: while i > 0, sum += tree[i], i -= i & (-i). Combines relevant nodes.

keyConcepts.name: Range Query
keyConcepts.description: Sum[l, r] = prefix(r) - prefix(l-1). Two queries give range sum in O(log n) each.

complexity.build: O(n log n) or O(n) optimized

algorithmSteps.description: Initialize BIT with 8 zeros. Index 0 unused (1-indexed).
Build BIT: Each position stores sum of its range of responsibility.
Query prefix sum [1, 4]: sum indices 4 → 0. Result: 3+2+(-1)+6 = 10
Query prefix sum [1, 7]: sum indices 7 → 6 → 4 → 0. Result: 16
Update index 3 by +5: Propagate to indices 3, 4, 8.
